title: The road to the Second World War
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:35Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-01T09:24:24Z autoreview: cleared with the fix (card wording)

match.reason: The new point covers the broader road to war, including aggression by Germany, Italy and Japan alongside appeasement, while the closest bank points cover only appeasement or only the 1939 Nazi-Soviet Pact and invasion of Poland, so none teaches the same idea at the same breadth.

draft.title: The road to the Second World War
card: In the 1930s, Japan, Italy and Germany used force or threats to expand their power. Japan invaded Manchuria in 1931. Italy invaded Ethiopia in 1935.
Germany under Hitler broke the Treaty of Versailles. It rearmed, moved troops into the Rhineland in 1936, joined with Austria in 1938 and took the Sudetenland from Czechoslovakia in 1938.
Britain and France gave in to some demands, hoping to avoid another war. At Munich in 1938, they agreed that Germany could take the Sudetenland.
In March 1939, Germany took the rest of Czechoslovakia. Germany invaded Poland on 1 September 1939, and Britain and France then declared war.
draft.remember: Aggression went unchecked as appeasement failed, until the invasion of Poland brought war.

a.q: What was the main aim of Britain and France in following appeasement?
opts: To avoid another war by giving in to some demands
To help Germany rebuild its army after Versailles
To prepare their own armies for an invasion of Germany
To win Italy and Japan over as allies against Germany
a.why: Appeasement meant giving in to some demands in the hope of keeping peace. It was not a plan to attack Germany, because Britain and France wanted to avoid war at that point.
a.clue: Think about what Munich in 1938 was meant to achieve.

b.q: Which event led directly to Britain and France declaring war on Germany in 1939?
opts: Germany's invasion of Poland
Germany's takeover of the Sudetenland
Italy's invasion of Ethiopia
Japan's invasion of Manchuria
b.why: Britain and France declared war after Germany invaded Poland on 1 September 1939. The Sudetenland was taken in 1938 with their agreement at Munich, so it is the tempting wrong option, but it did not lead to war then.
b.clue: Look for the event that came just before the declarations of war.

a.best: To avoid another war by giving in to some demands

problems.detail: "Joined with Austria in 1938" can read as a voluntary merger. The Anschluss was an annexation: German troops marched in under threat. Something like "took over Austria" or "annexed Austria" would fit the card's own point about force or threats.

check.summary: The facts, dates and both questions are sound, and each question has one clear answer. One small wording issue: "joined with Austria" softens what was a forced annexation (the Anschluss).
